recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future Vocab work may choose different clinical example content, as the 2018 minutes anticipated, but FHIR-17402 itself is already applied in current source and does not require another core spec edit.
issue_request: FHIR-17402 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification Vocab change request raised against STU3 terminology guidance. It asked for a concrete JSON/XML example showing how to add a value with an extensible binding and for a clearer explanation of extensible binding behavior; the accepted resolution was to add a better example on its own page.
initial_application: The Jira comments record application in svn 14745, 14766, 14787, 14790, 14791, and 14792. In git history these appear as 2420a34ab2, cc33213f90, 1c42a3bd45, 8c0b9717d6, ef8158a704, and 9c977328a2; 1c42a3bd45 added source/terminologies-binding-examples.html with Extensible and Preferred binding examples and linked the page from source/terminologies.html, and 9c977328a2 made follow-up wording and logic updates.
additional_context: source/hierarchy.xml includes terminologies-binding-examples.html under the active Terminology page tree, and source/terminologies.html links the Extensible Binding Strength section to that examples page. The current examples page still contains the local-code extensible-binding case and the follow-up instance showing the local code as an additional Coding alongside the applicable SNOMED CT code. Later examples-page work for FHIR-38967 completed other binding-strength examples without reversing the FHIR-17402 extensible-binding guidance. Vocab minutes on 2018-08-20 reviewed the updated extensible-binding examples and noted possible future refinements, but no current source or community evidence found in this investigation supersedes the applied result.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because no source edit is needed. The current build-scope source already has the standalone Terminology Binding Examples page requested by the issue, the Using Codes page links to it, and the extensible-binding examples demonstrate when a local code is not valid by itself and when it may be sent as an additional Coding.
